title: Heat the ammonia maker
hook: Heat speeds reactions up. Does it also leave more product at the end?

knows: that heating speeds reactions up (twice-as-hot-not-twice-as-fast, the-tail-that-reacts)
that an equilibrium settles where forward and backward rates match (four-to-one-settles)
doesNotKnow: that temperature changes the equilibrium constant itself
that for a reaction that releases heat, heating lowers how much product there is at the end

misconception: Heating helps every reaction, so a hotter ammonia reactor ends with more ammonia.
objective: The learner can say that heating the ammonia reaction from 25 °C to 450 °C lowers K by a factor of billions, and explain that because making ammonia releases heat, heating pushes the balance back, even though it makes the reaction faster.

claims.text: N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3 releases heat: ΔH° about −92 kJ/mol, with ΔS° about −198 J/(mol K) at 25 °C (question: 'releases heat'; reveal: 'Making ammonia releases heat').
claims.source: CODATA Key Values / CRC Handbook standard thermodynamic properties: ΔfH NH3(g) −45.94 kJ/mol; S° NH3(g) 192.77, N2 191.61, H2 130.68 J/(mol K). ΔH° = 2(−45.94) = −91.88 kJ/mol; ΔS° = 385.54 − 191.61 − 392.04 = −198.11 J/(mol K) (node, demo-builder 2026-10-14). Demo.tsx DH, DS. Brief claim 1.
claims.note: Opened: NASA TM-4513 polynomials (McBride, Gordon & Reno 1993; Cantera data/nasa_gas.yaml) give exactly the CODATA values at 298.15 K: NH3 -45.94 kJ/mol and 192.77, N2 191.61, H2 130.68 J/(mol K). Also CRC (-45.9, 192.8) and JANAF (-45.898, 192.774). Node: dH = -91.88 kJ/mol, dS = -198.11 J/(mol K).

claims.text: With ΔH° and ΔS° varying with temperature (full NASA TM-4513 data), K is about 5.6 × 10^5 at 25 °C, about 0.39 at 200 °C and about 4.9 × 10^-5 at 450 °C, a fall by a factor of billions (about 10^10) (stage dot labels '5.6 × 10⁵', '0.39', '4.9 × 10⁻⁵'; reveal: 'K fell from about 5.6 × 10⁵ at 25 °C to about 4.9 × 10⁻⁵ at 450 °C, a factor of billions').
claims.source: NASA-7 polynomials, McBride, Gordon & Reno, NASA TM-4513 (1993), as transcribed in Cantera data/nasa_gas.yaml (NH3, N2, H2; 200-1000 K range). ΔG°(T) = 2G(NH3) − G(N2) − 3G(H2) from the polynomials; K = exp(−ΔG°/RT): K = 5.60e5, 0.391, 4.91e-5; ratio 1.1e10 (node, demo-builder 2026-10-14, from Demo.tsx kAt()). At 25 °C the polynomials give ΔH° = −91.88 kJ/mol, ΔS° = −198.1 J/(mol K) (claim 1); at 450 °C ΔH° = −105.9 kJ/mol. Brief claim 2.
claims.note: v2 (2026-10-14, W-674): switched from constant 25 °C ΔH°/ΔS° (0.62, 1.9e-4; disputed, no caveat on stage) to the full-data K the fact-checker computed from NASA TM-4513. Needs a fresh check.

claims.text: Starting from 1 N2 : 3 H2 at 1 bar total, ammonia is about 94% of the settled gas at 25 °C, about 15% at 200 °C and about 0.23% at 450 °C (stage bar 'NH₃ at the end, 25 °C: 94%' etc.).
claims.source: Ideal-gas equilibrium with the K of claim 2: K = x_NH3² / (x_N2 · x_H2³) at P = 1 bar = P°; with extent ξ, K = 4ξ²(4 − 2ξ)² / (27(1 − ξ)⁴), solved by bisection; share 2ξ/(4 − 2ξ) = 0.938, 0.148, 0.0023 (node, demo-builder 2026-10-14; Demo.tsx shareAt()). Not in the brief: added so the 'ammonia at the end' in the question is drawn, not only K. The 1 bar condition shows on the locked bar label only.
claims.note: v2 (2026-10-14, W-674): shares now from the full-data K of claim 2 (were 17% and 0.45% under constant ΔH°/ΔS°; disputed). Needs a fresh check.

claims.text: For a reaction that releases heat, raising the temperature lowers K (reveal: 'so heat pushes the balance back toward nitrogen and hydrogen'); large K means mostly product at equilibrium (stage caption 'large K: mostly ammonia').
claims.source: van 't Hoff: d ln K / dT = ΔH°/(RT²) < 0 when ΔH° < 0 (Atkins & de Paula, Physical Chemistry, equilibrium chapter). Brief claim 3.
claims.note: Derivation: in the lesson's model ln K = -dH/RT + dS/R, so d ln K/dT = dH/RT^2 < 0 when dH < 0 (van 't Hoff). The full NASA data agree (K falls at every temperature). 'Large K: mostly ammonia' is shown by c3's calculation (K = 5.6e5 gives 94% NH3 at 1 bar from a 1:3 feed).

claims.text: Heating makes the reaction reach equilibrium faster (stage label 'reaches equilibrium faster' beside the 450 °C dot; reveal: 'Heat still makes the reaction faster').
claims.source: Arrhenius: k = A exp(−Ea/RT) rises with T for forward and backward steps (Atkins & de Paula, Physical Chemistry, reaction kinetics). Qualitative; no number shown.
claims.note: Held: I could not open the cited Atkins kinetics chapter, or any other source on the rate of ammonia synthesis against temperature (web blocked). Arrhenius behaviour with a positive activation energy is an empirical fact about this reaction and cannot be derived from the thermodynamic data I did open. To verify it, give me an openable source for the temperature dependence of the ammonia-synthesis rate (or a general Arrhenius statement).

claims.text: Industrial ammonia plants (Haber-Bosch) run hot anyway, with an iron catalyst and high pressure to win some yield back (reveal).
claims.source: Greenwood & Earnshaw, Chemistry of the Elements, nitrogen chapter (ammonia synthesis: about 400-450 °C, about 150-300 bar, iron catalyst). Brief claim 4: if no source is checkable, cut the 'factories' sentence from the reveal and keep the rest.
claims.note: Held: Greenwood & Earnshaw (or any source on industrial Haber-Bosch conditions) could not be opened. Only the 'high pressure wins yield back' part can be derived (4 mol of gas -> 2 mol, so at fixed K the ammonia mole fraction rises with P); 'factories run hot with an iron catalyst' cannot. The brief says to cut the factories sentence if no source can be checked. Cut it (cm-chemistry's call), or supply an openable source.

claims.text: Temperature is the one change that moves K itself (reveal): for a given reaction, K depends only on temperature; pressure, concentration and catalysts shift or speed the mixture but leave K alone.
claims.source: Atkins & de Paula, Physical Chemistry, chemical equilibrium (K = exp(−ΔrG°/RT), and ΔrG° depends only on T for a fixed standard state); the same point is made in squeeze-the-brown-gas and lower-the-hill.
claims.note: Derivation: K = exp(-dG°/RT), and dG° for a fixed reaction and standard state depends only on T. Pressure and concentration enter Q, not K. A catalyst changes neither the reactant nor the product states, so dG° and K are unchanged (thermodynamic K, in fugacities).

recall.question: A reaction gives out heat. You run it hotter. What happens to the amount of product once it settles, and to how fast it gets there?
recall.why: Heat lowers K for a reaction that releases heat, so less product at the end, while every step still speeds up. Hotter trades yield for speed.
